topic.title: Enforcing Terminology and Glossaries
topic.shortdesc: How to supply a terminology list so the agent uses consistent, approved translations for key terms.

body.p: Product names, feature names, and other fixed terms need to be translated the same way every time they appear.

section.title: Providing a Terminology List
section.p: If you already know which terms need a fixed translation, list them in a file and tell the agent to use that file in agent-instructions.md. The agent can read a terminology file in any format, including one exported from an existing terminology tool, as long as agent-instructions.md explains how to read it. Include a representative snippet of the file in your instructions so the agent knows what to expect.
To keep costs down, the agent reads only the line ranges it needs rather than the whole file, so keep each entry on its own line.
For example, you can add instructions like these to agent-instructions.md, embedding a snippet of your TBX (TermBase eXchange) terminology file:

p.codeblock:
When you need to translate a term, search in [the terms file](./terms.tbx) and use the canonical translation found there instead of re-translating.
The file has entries with this format:
<termEntry id="review-task"> <langSet xml:lang="en"><tig><term>review task</term></tig></langSet> <langSet xml:lang="fr-FR"><tig><term>tâche de révision</term></tig></langSet> <langSet xml:lang="de-DE"><tig><term>Prüfaufgabe</term></tig></langSet> </termEntry>
Use your grep tool to search it.

section.title: Letting the Agent Build the List
section.p: If you want the agent to also update the terms file or build it if you do not have one, you can add instructions along these lines to agent-instructions.md:

p.codeblock: Whenever you translate a topic, identify terms (product names, feature names, UI labels) and record them, together with the translation you used, in [the terms file](./terms.tbx).

section.p: Over time this produces a project-specific glossary without you having to prepare one up front. Review the terminology file after each translation task and correct any entries the agent got wrong; corrected entries are picked up the same way on later jobs.
